records.name: Seed Multiplication Scheme of Paddy
records.parent_programme: Assistance to the farmers for quality seed production
records.summary: Paddy seed multiplication scheme, listed under assistance to the farmers for quality seed production, in which farmers who produce and supply seeds to the Department of Agriculture on Contract basis can enroll and register their seed farms. An incentive is provided for all the seeds produced by the farmers, with a Paddy Premium of Rs.2/- per Kg of seed for the production of Certified class seeds.
records.benefits: In order to encourage the farmers and to offset the special efforts taken by them, incentive is provided for all the seeds produced by the farmers. Paddy Premium for the production of Certified class seeds: Rs.2/- per Kg of seed.
records.eligibility: All farmers who produce and supply the seeds to the Department of Agriculture on Contract basis are eligible to enroll and register their seed farms under this programme. Preference will be given to farm women groups, Farmers Interest Groups. The required source seed will be supplied by the Department of Agriculture through the Agricultural Extension Centres on payment. The farmers should follow the guidelines given by the field level functionaries / Seed Certification officers to maintain the Quality.
records.how_to_apply: Eligible farmers enroll and register their seed farms under this programme.
records.contact_officers: Assistant Agricultural officer at the Village Level; Assistant Seed Officer / Deputy Agricultural Officer / Agricultural Officer at the Block Level; The Assistant Director of Agriculture at the Block Level; The Joint Director of Agriculture at the District Level

records.summary: Tamil Nadu's Cereals Development Programme for paddy, listed under the Macro Management Mode schemes for increasing crop productivity, has three components: a seed subsidy through the seed village concept, demonstrations on System of Rice Intensification, and Integrated Pest Management demonstration cum training (Farmers Field School). records.name: Seed Village Scheme
records.summary: The Seed Village Scheme is a Tamil Nadu agriculture scheme under which Foundation / Certified seeds of Paddy are distributed at 50% cost for the production of quality seeds by farmers. It also covers a three-day training on seed production technology for farmers who receive seeds from the department at 50% cost, and the supply of storage bins to farmers.
records.benefits: Distribution of Foundation / Certified seeds of Paddy at 50% cost for the production of quality seeds by farmers. Three Days Training on seed production technology in three important phases of the crops to farmers who receive seeds from the department @ 50% cost for production of quality Seeds. 50 farmers per training totally 8000 training per year. Supply of Storage Bin to the farmers, with two sets of amounts: first set Rs.3000/- for 20 qtl bin and Rs.1500/- for 10 qtl. bin (or) 33% cost of bin; second set Rs.2000/- for 20 qtl bin and Rs.1000/- for 10 qtl. bin (or) 25% cost of bin; beneficiary category not stated on the page.
records.eligibility: All the farmers in the State who are willing to produce quality seeds from their lands for their own use and for distribution to other farmers.
records.contact_officers: Seed distribution: Assistant Agricultural officer at the Village Level. Training: Assistant seed officer /Deputy Agricultural Officer / Agricultural Officer at the Block Level. Storage bin: The Assistant Director of Agriculture at the Block Level (listed with the first set of amounts); The Joint Director of Agriculture at the District Level (listed with the second set of amounts).

records.name: Agricultural Mechanisation Programme
records.summary: The Agricultural Mechanisation Programme provides subsidy assistance to farmers for procuring agricultural machinery and implements such as Tractors, Power Tillers, Self propelled Paddy Transplanters, Self propelled paddy reapers, Rotavator, Cultivator, Disc Plough, Chisel Plough etc. The subsidy is 25% of the cost of machinery / implements or the ceiling limit prescribed by Government of India for each machinery / implement, whichever is less, and the project area is All Districts (Except Chennai).

records.name: Rain Water Harvesting and Runoff Management Programme
records.summary: Rain water harvesting and runoff management programme for all districts except Chennai and Nilgiris, presented on the page together with the NABARD assisted Rain Water Harvesting Programme. Listed works are percolation ponds; major, medium and minor check dams; farm ponds; rejuvenation of unused wells; and village tanks / Ooranies, with a 100% grant on works in community lands (beneficiaries also contribute a share in cash) and a 90% subsidy on works in patta lands (remaining 10% is beneficiary share).
records.benefits: 100% grant is provided on cost of works taken up in community lands. However, the beneficiaries are required to contribute 10% of the cost of works (it is 5% in case of SC/ST) in cash which will be deposited in the name of the Village Development Association / Watershed Association for future maintenance of the assets created. 90% subsidy is provided on cost of works in patta lands and the remaining 10% is collected as beneficiary share.
records.funding_pattern: Community lands: 100% grant on cost of works; beneficiaries to contribute 10% of the cost of works (5% in case of SC/ST) in cash. Patta lands: 90% subsidy on cost of works; remaining 10% collected as beneficiary share.

records.name: Crop Insurance Scheme
records.summary: State Government-sponsored crop insurance scheme in Kerala for farmers facing production risks on various counts, such as drought, floods, etc.; a crop insurance scheme with contribution from the participating farmers has been in operation covering 25 major crops grown in the state since 1995. The present scheme aims at revamping the crop insurance programme making it viable so as to cater to risk coverage of small and marginal farmers, with an outlay of Rs.100.00 lakhs.

records.name: National Agricultural Insurance Scheme (NAIS)
records.funding_pattern: 50:50 sharing basis between central and state government.
records.implementing_agency: Agriculture Department; the NAIS scheme is implemented by the Agricultural Insurance Corporation
records.summary: National Agricultural Insurance Scheme (NAIS) in Kerala, sponsored by both the Central and State Government, which aims at tackling the issue of production risk faced by the agricultural sector. The Rs.1.50 crores allocated for the scheme will be utilised as 50 percent contribution of the State (excluding salary component) towards the NAIS implemented by the Agricultural Insurance Corporation for crops such as paddy, banana, tapioca, ginger, turmeric and pineapple.

records.summary: A special central assistance scheme of the Government of India, implemented by the Government of Kerala, primarily aimed at evolving a strategy to rejuvenate the agriculture sector of the State. Its general objective is to provide incentives to the State for increasing public investment in agriculture and allied sectors, and the allocation for the scheme is Rs.6011.10 lakhs.

records.name: Minimum Support Price Scheme
records.implementing_agency: National Agricultural Co-operative Marketing Federation (NAFED), which in the procurement operation appoints state level agencies in consultation with the State Governments who in turn involve their co-operative marketing societies for the procurement at the field level
records.summary: Price support scheme that ensures farmers a minimum support price, worked out by the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) set up by the Government of India, and safeguards farmers' interest especially during periods of high production and crash in price. The page lists the 2010-11 minimum support price for paddy as 1000 (Common) and 1030 (Grade 'A'), with no unit stated.
records.benefits: Ensures farmers a minimum support price, which is worked out by the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) set up by the Government of India. As described on the page, a minimum price is established by a government and supported by payments to producers in the event that the market price falls below the specified minimum price; a price support scheme can also be an agreement where the government agrees to purchase the surplus at a minimum price. This scheme safeguards the farmers' interest especially during periods of high production and crash in price. Minimum support price (2010-11) for Paddy: Common 1000; Grade 'A' 1030 (unit not stated on the page). Example given on the page: if a price floor were set in place for paddy, the government would be forced to purchase the resulting surplus from the paddy farmers (thereby subsidizing the farmers) and store or otherwise dispose it.
